clue.text: Take drugs, emaciated, drawn, shabby

parts.note: to 'do gear' is slang for taking drugs, gear being drugs

indicators.note: drawn as in drained or emptied: the inside of the word is pulled out, leaving its two ends

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A grim portrait of an addict: using drugs, wasted away, haggard and down at heel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emaciated' and 'drawn' look like more adjectives in a list of symptoms; 'drawn' actually empties 'emaciated' to ED.
explanation.definitionFit: A book with turned-down page corners is worn and tatty, so the word is used for anything well-thumbed and scruffy.

clue.text: Fine food store McCartney regularly sampled

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop selling fine foods

indicators.note: regularly sampled means every other letter of the name is taken

parts.note: its even-numbered letters

explanation.surface: Paul McCartney tasting his way round a fine-food shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine here means dainty or exquisite, as in fine lace or fine workmanship.

clue.text: Bemused solvers' call for help Julius has answered 32 times?

definitions.text: Bemused solvers' call for help Julius has answered 32 times?

parts.words: Bemused solvers' call for help Julius has answered 32 times?
parts.note: the stuck solver's plea is the phrase, and the setter has met it by writing one clue for each entry in this grid

explanation.walkthrough: Julius is the setter of this puzzle; the phrase is also the title of an old British TV charades game show.
explanation.definitionFit: Puzzled solvers ask for a hint, and the setter responds by supplying each of the puzzle's clues.

clue.text: Last station announcement?

parts.note: at the final stop of a railway line every passenger must get off, and staff call this out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' suggests a closing or farewell announcement; it is the terminus of a train route.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the standard British railway call telling everyone to leave the train at the end of the line.

clue.text: Spain claiming penny in tax upset economic migrant

indicators.note: claiming means the country's code lays hold of the remaining letters that follow it

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for penny within the turned word for tax
upset in a down clue means the word for tax is turned upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Spain demands a penny more in tax, which annoys a foreign worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the migrant's mood but reverses TAX to XAT, which takes P to give XPAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An expatriate is someone living abroad, often having moved there for work or a better income.

clue.text: 0-0 in Paris — time to find one's correct position

parts.note: the first 0 is the letter O; the second is 'nothing', which in Paris (in French) is RIEN

explanation.surface: A goalless draw in a French match, then time for a team to regroup in its proper formation.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen makes it look like a football score; read the first nought as the letter O and the second as French 'rien', meaning nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To orient yourself is to work out where you are and which way you face, getting your bearings.

clue.text: Mature nurse sustaining tear

indicators.note: sustaining means holding up, so in this down clue the nurse sits beneath the tear

parts.note: a rip is a tear
EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: An experienced nurse holding back a tear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear' looks like crying, but it is a rip in fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit or cheese that ripens comes to maturity, so the verb means to mature.

clue.text: Electronic vehicle drained the night before the festival

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

indicators.note: drained means the inside of the word is emptied out, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An electric car runs out of charge just before the holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas Eve is the evening before Christmas, so eve means the day or night before a feast.

clue.text: Box Victor in upcoming challenge

indicators.note: in places the radio code letter inside the turned word
upcoming in a down clue means the word for challenge reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a test is a challenge
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A boxer named Victor in a forthcoming bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a sport; it is British slang for a television.
explanation.definitionFit: The box is informal British slang for the television.

clue.text: Old soldiers check trap which has been set up

parts.note: to vet is to check

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means turned upwards, so the word for trap reads backwards

parts.note: a snare is a trap

explanation.surface: Former servicemen inspect a trap that someone has laid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' sounds like laying a trap; in a down clue it turns SNARE upward into ERANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Veterans are people who served in the armed forces long ago.

clue.text: Make even draw around about 7

indicators.note: around signals that the turned word wraps itself round the answer to clue 7
about signals that the word for draw is turned back to front

parts.note: to draw is to pull
the answer to 7 down, the night before a festival

explanation.surface: Equalise the scores by drawing at around seven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' looks like a time but is a cross-reference to the answer of 7 down; 'around' and 'about' are two separate signals, one wrapping and one turning.
explanation.definitionFit: To level up is to raise the lower side so both stand equal, making things even.

clue.text: State former President beginning to struggle

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: beginning to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A politician recounts how an ex-President started to falter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a noun, a country; here it is a verb, to say.
explanation.definitionFit: To express something is to put it into words, to say or declare it.

clue.text: Caught touchy setter stripping off for bed

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: stripping off takes the outer layer from each of the two words, leaving only their insides

parts.note: its middle letters
its middle letters

explanation.surface: A sensitive crossword setter is caught undressing for bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripping off' works on both 'touchy' and 'setter', removing the first and last letters of each to leave OUCH and ETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A couchette is a sleeping berth on a continental train, so a bed of a particular kind.

clue.text: Thing coming out after dark?

indicators.note: coming out suggests the word thing emerges in a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A spooky question about some creature that emerges once it gets dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after dark' reads as one phrase, but only 'dark' is the definition; 'after' joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark is a common way of naming nighttime, the hours without daylight.

clue.text: Family history buff got lineages wrong

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters of got lineages are out of their correct order

explanation.surface: A family historian has made errors in their ancestral lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A genealogist researches ancestry and traces lineages, the very study of family history.

clue.text: Extra incentive to board public transport?

indicators.note: to board is to get on, so the answer sits on board, inside the words extra incentive

explanation.surface: A commuter scheme offering a bonus to get people onto buses and trains.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway service is one of the main forms of public transport available to anyone with a ticket.

clue.text: Intently looking around, very hungry

indicators.note: around means the word for looking intently is wrapped round the abbreviation for very

parts.note: staring means looking intently

explanation.surface: Someone peering intently all around, desperate for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Starving is used informally for being ravenous, extremely in need of a meal.

clue.text: Wholesale store's opening certain branches like this?

indicators.note: opening means only the first letter of the word store is used

parts.note: its first letter
weeping describes trees such as the weeping willow, whose branches droop

explanation.surface: A wholesale store opens some new branches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'branches' looks like a chain of shops, but these are the drooping boughs of a weeping willow.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeping changes are wholesale ones, broad and indiscriminate in their reach.

clue.text: Groups at the front cycling round the back of 15 perhaps

indicators.note: cycling round means the two-word phrase rotates, its last part moving to the front

parts.note: the carriage at the back of a train, where the guard rides, is the guard's van

explanation.surface: Cyclists' leading groups riding round the rear of a train.
explanation.walkthrough: '15' refers to 15 across, TRAIN; its rear carriage is the GUARD'S VAN, and VAN moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The vanguard is the leading part of an army or movement, so vanguards are groups at the head.

clue.text: Cost of training?

parts.note: training here is travelling by train, and its cost is the ticket price

explanation.walkthrough: 'training' suggests the fee for a course; read it as going by train.
explanation.definitionFit: The ticket price for a journey on the railway is what you pay to go by train.

clue.text: Moles which are found under the tracks?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: spies planted long in advance who lie dormant until activated

definitions.text: which are found under the tracks?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the wooden or concrete beams laid under railway lines

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests burrowing animals beneath the railway; in Britain the cross-beams that support rails are called sleepers (Americans say ties).
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-cover agents wait inactive for years, and railway beams lie flat beneath the rails, both being sleepers.

clue.text: African animal area located between two major US cities

indicators.note: located between means the area's letter sits in the gap between the two city abbreviations

parts.note: NY is New York and LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A zoo's African beast living somewhere between two big American cities.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa.

clue.text: Give birth with assistance

parts.note: help means assistance

explanation.surface: A mother delivers her baby with the help of a midwife.
explanation.definitionFit: Whelping is the verb used for a dog or similar animal bringing forth puppies.

clue.text: Coach women's American golf organisation discharged

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: discharged means emptied, so the word loses its contents and keeps its two ends

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A women's coach is dismissed by an American golfing body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a sports trainer; it is a horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach in the old sense is a horse-drawn carriage, and a wagon is a similar wheeled vehicle.

clue.text: Masterpiece debut of artist (after Mondrian)

indicators.note: after means the first letter of artist follows the painter's first name

parts.note: the first name of Mondrian, the Dutch abstract painter of grids and primary colours

indicators.note: debut of means the first letter of the word artist

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: An artist's first great work, made under Mondrian's influence.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like an art-history aside; in fact it supplies PIET, Mondrian's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a painting or sculpture of Mary holding the dead Christ; Michelangelo's is a celebrated masterwork.

clue.text: Playing piano, Ute Lemper's intro is rich, earthy, fluid

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters being performed in a fresh arrangement, like improvised music
intro means just the opening letter of the singer's name is used

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A review of the cabaret singer Ute Lemper at the piano, her opening rich and earthy and flowing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ute Lemper is a German singer, which makes this read like a concert review; the three adjectives together describe the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundnut cooking oil is a liquid with a rich, nutty, earthy taste.

clue.text: Poet's adult nude sculpture

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: sculpture suggests the letters of nude are moulded into a new shape

explanation.surface: A poet's grown-up nude statue.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was an Anglo-American twentieth-century poet.

clue.text: Imperial unit capturing European vessel

indicators.note: capturing means the unit of volume holds the abbreviation for European inside it

parts.note: a gallon is a unit of volume in the British imperial system

explanation.surface: A naval tale of an imperial force seizing a European ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large sailing ship of the 16th to 18th centuries, so a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Drunk subaltern going round island

indicators.note: going round means the officer's abbreviation surrounds the letter for island

parts.note: a subaltern is a junior officer such as a lieutenant, abbreviated Lt

explanation.surface: A tipsy junior officer staggering round an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit is informal slang for intoxicated.

clue.text: The German raid injured Francophone philosopher

parts.note: der is a German word for the

indicators.note: injured suggests the word raid is damaged and its letters knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A wartime story of a German air raid wounding a French thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Derrida was the French-language thinker who founded deconstruction.

clue.text: When flying, don't be taking British Airways — it's only reasonable

indicators.note: be taking means the word don't takes in the airline's initials
flying suggests the letters scatter and land in a new order

parts.note: taken without the apostrophe
BA is the airline's abbreviation

explanation.surface: Advice for a trip: avoid British Airways, which is merely tolerable.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is not bad means it is fair or acceptable, decent enough.

clue.text: Liqueur established during a 13 in America?

indicators.note: during means the word for established falls in the middle of the other letters

parts.note: the answer to 13 across spelt the informal American way
set means established, as in set in its ways

explanation.surface: A cocktail drunk on an evening out in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: '13' is a cross-reference to 13 across; 'in America' asks for its informal American spelling, as on diner signs.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet aniseed-flavoured French spirit drunk after meals.
